text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000321 bills 99215 well above its risk-adjusted expectation, with over half of those claims on low-complexity patients, but records came back for too few claims to confirm or rule out upcoding.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The claims pattern leans toward concern. 99215 rates run above the all-provider share in every complexity band, and the excess is not confined to sicker patients. The low-complexity sample includes 99215s for single acute or minor diagnoses such as upper respiratory infection, abdominal pain, rash and UTI (e.g., C0170304, C0171045, C0171804, C0172506). The high-complexity sample (e.g., C0171316, C0170529) looks plausibly consistent with the billed level. The documentation cannot settle the question: only 3 documented 99215 claims came back, all supported at high MDM, and the 2 data-reviewed notes with no lab or test line are only weak evidence of inflated notes. A reviewer should first request charts specifically for the low-complexity 99215 claims listed, starting with the single-acute-diagnosis visits, to see whether the documented MDM supports level 5 or reads as templated."}
